picks.title: Amazon's new Alexa tablets include a 12-inch model with anti-glare screen
picks.rationale: Amazon launches three new tablets built around Alexa+, its first hardware line rebranded around the AI assistant: a concrete product launch where AI is the selling point.
picks.excerpt: Amazon has launched three new tablets that come with Alexa+.

picks.title: Natura’s $99 smart ring puts AI agents on your finger
picks.rationale: A $99 ring that summons AI agents with a finger press to run tasks, capture thoughts and control devices: a new form factor for agent input, and a cheap one.
picks.excerpt: Natura’s $99 Interface smart ring lets you summon AI agents with the press of a finger to complete tasks, capture thoughts, and control devices — while doubling as a health tracker.

picks.title: Apple is set to show off new smart home devices at an October 13 event
picks.rationale: Apple officially announces its 'Welcome Home' event for Oct 13, where a Siri/Apple Intelligence home hub is expected: the official date turns last month's rumor into a scheduled launch.
picks.excerpt: Apple teased a 'Welcome Home' event for October 13 at 9AM ET, where it is expected to show new smart home devices such as a Siri/Apple Intelligence-driven home hub.

picks.title: Nvidia's big bet on physical AI aims for safer robotaxis, humanoid robots
picks.rationale: Nvidia's full-stack safety system for physical AI, already used by robotics makers such as Agility: the layer that decides whether humanoids and robotaxis can be trusted around people.
picks.excerpt: Full-stack safety solution for physical AI is being used by robotics companies.

picks.title: This $1599 smart monitor robotic arm has its own built-in PC, and its 27-inch 4K display will follow you around thanks to its binocular 3D sensor
picks.rationale: CyboPal's monitor on a robotic arm uses an on-device NPU for face tracking, gesture recognition and 3D sensing so the screen follows the user: on-device AI changing desk ergonomics.
picks.excerpt: CyboPal's $1,599 smart monitor sits on a robotic arm with a built-in Rockchip RK3588 (6 TOPS NPU) 'Linux AI Compute Base' that handles on-device face tracking, gesture recognition and 3D spatial sensing so the 27-inch 4K display follows the user.

https://www.engadget.com/2281263/apple-i.new_action: Apple officially announced its 'Welcome Home' event for October 13 at 9AM ET; the 09-22 card was only a report that the device might come next month.
